cards.explanation: The answer is that they preach the word. Verse 4 says, “Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.” Scattered, and still preaching the word wherever they went, friends. When I got shoved into a junk drawer, all I did was gather dust.
The answer is Christ. Verse 5 says Philip, one of the scattered believers, “…proclaimed the Christ to them.” He went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ, friends.

The answer is the signs they see him perform. Verse 6 says the crowds paid close attention “…to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.” They heard it and they saw it. That's a crowd with its eyes AND its ears wide open.

The answer is False. The verse says, “With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed…” (Acts 8:7). Those spirits did NOT leave quietly, friends. Whatever happened in that city, you could hear it.

The answer is joy. Verse 8 says, “So there was great joy in that city.” Unclean spirits came out of many, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed. I think that city had the best day it had ever had.

The answer is sorcery. Acts 8:9 says Simon “…had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria.” He had that city's attention before Philip ever walked in. Remember that, friends, because it matters later in the story.

The answer is The Great Power. The people said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.” (Acts 8:10). From the least to the greatest, they all heeded his words. That's a big name to hang on one man.

The answer is False. Acts 8:11 says the people paid close attention to him because “…he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.” That's a long-running habit, not a brand new fan club. Simon had been the talk of the city long before Philip showed up.

The answer is baptized. Acts 8:12 says, “…they were baptized, both men and women.” They believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ. Belief came first, then baptism, friends.

The answer is the great signs and miracles. Verse 13 says Simon “…followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.” This is the same Simon who had astounded people for a long time (Acts 8:11). Now the shoe is on the other foot, and I bet it felt strange.

The answers are Peter and John. Verse 14 says the apostles in Jerusalem “…sent Peter and John to them.” Peter is one of the apostles, and he's named right alongside John. They're sent to Samaria as a pair, friends.
The answer is the Holy Spirit. Acts 8:15 says that on their arrival, Peter and John prayed “…for them to receive the Holy Spirit.” The Spirit is what that prayer was about, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.” (Acts 8:16). Not many, not some, none yet. Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:17).

The answer is money. Acts 8:18 says that when Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, “…he offered them money.” Peter answers that Simon thought he could buy the gift of God with money. I think that's the moment the room got awkward.

The answer is the power to give the Holy Spirit. Simon said, “Give me this power as well… so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit” (Acts 8:19). He wanted to be the one handing it out. Peter's answer comes next, friends.

The answer is gift. Peter says, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!” (Acts 8:20). A gift can't be bought, friends. That's the whole point of a gift.

The answer is that his heart is not right before God. Peter tells Simon, “You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.” (Acts 8:21). It's about his heart. I think that's a hard thing to hear.
The answer is forgive. Peter says, “Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.” (Acts 8:22). He had just told Simon to repent and pray to the Lord. The door is still open, friends.
The answer is True. Simon says, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.” (Acts 8:24). He's asking for prayer after what Peter said to him. I think he's rattled.

The answer is that they preach the gospel. Acts 8:25 says they returned to Jerusalem, “…preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages.” They were not coasting home, friends. The trip back turned into a preaching tour.
